The bug in [`Partial.with(DateTimeFieldType, int)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_4_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/Partial.java#L426-L474) has been fixed.

### Root Cause
In [`Partial.with(DateTimeFieldType, int)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_4_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/Partial.java#L464), when creating the new [`Partial`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_4_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/Partial.java) instance after inserting a new field, it called the package-private constructor `Partial(Chronology, DateTimeFieldType[], int[])` instead of the public validating constructor [`Partial(DateTimeFieldType[], int[], Chronology)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_4_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/Partial.java#L189-L249). The package-private constructor performs no validation, allowing conflicting or duplicate fields (such as `hourOfDay` and `clockhourOfDay`) to be added.

### Solution
Updated the constructor invocation in [`Partial.with`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_4_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/Partial.java#L464) to call `new Partial(newTypes, newValues, iChronology)`, which performs full duplicate and ordering validations.
